editions.label: 15 Sep
editions.title: Greater Lisbon building permits crash 35% — yet prices keep rising
editions.summary: Portugal's construction pipeline is thinning at the top. Licensed buildings fell 7.1% in Q2, with Greater Lisbon down a startling 35.1%, even as new-dwelling permits crept up 10.8%. Yet prices refuse to cool: Lisbon has shed 8,300 short-term lets since the pandemic — a 41% cull — and values still rose. Institutional capital is leaning in anyway: Davidson Kempner, ECS Capital and Magna Industrial just launched a logistics JV anchored by a 630,000 m² site near Lisbon. And Brussels has effectively endorsed Portugal's €10bn public-housing push. Net: the supply-demand gap is the trade — and the smart money is positioning around it.

editions.label: 14 Sep
editions.title: Home permits fall 7%, Lisbon licensing down 35% — Portugal's supply squeeze tightens
editions.summary: Portugal's housing math isn't adding up. Building permits fell 7.1% year-on-year in Q2 and completions dropped 4.2% — even as the government calls new supply 'urgent.' The squeeze is worst where demand is hottest: licensing crashed 35.1% in Greater Lisbon and 24.9% in the Algarve. Meanwhile more than half of Portuguese municipalities are now formally under housing pressure. For anyone who can actually deliver units, scarcity is the whole game — Belfoz reserved all 66 Foz do Porto flats in ~45 days. Net: capital is plentiful and permits are not; execution and land are the moat.

editions.label: 13 Sep
editions.title: ECB hikes to 2.5%: pricier money for Portugal's builders as prime demand runs red-hot
editions.summary: The ECB lifted its deposit rate to 2.5% on Wednesday, an energy-fed move that makes construction and acquisition finance costlier for Portuguese developers and funds. Yet demand for the right product is undimmed: ZFC Invest's €60M Belfoz in Foz do Porto reserved all 66 units in about 45 days. Logistics vacancy sits near 1.8% in Lisbon and 0.5% in Porto, forcing occupiers into build-to-suit deals. And landlords just won headroom to raise rents up to 2.56% in 2027. Net: the cost of capital is rising, but scarcity — of quality space and of new supply — is doing the heavy lifting on pricing.

editions.label: 12 Sep
editions.title: Davidson Kempner, ECS launch Iberian logistics JV at 630,000 m² Benavente hub
editions.summary: ECS Capital and Davidson Kempner have formed a joint venture with builder Magna Industrial to develop logistics across Iberia. Their first move is the Benavente Prime Hub — 630,000 m² of land and 380,000 m² of built space over seven phases, breaking ground this year. It's a clear vote of confidence in Portugal's nearshoring and e-commerce story. Elsewhere the pressure on tenants tightened: INE set the 2027 rent coefficient at 2.56%, the second-highest in a decade. And capital keeps hunting yield — Homely Capital is weighing €100M of tourist apartments that would include Lisbon. Net: institutional money is leaning hard into Portuguese logistics and rental income, even as households feel the squeeze.

editions.label: 11 Sep
editions.title: Portugal property splits two ways: €1.41bn invested as Euribor nears 3%
editions.summary: Portugal's property market is running at two speeds — and the gap is widening. Commercial investment hit €1.41 billion in the first half, up 14% — but the money is crowding into hotels and retail while offices weaken. Foreign capital drove 65% of it. Residential prices keep climbing — Lisbon now €5,850/m², up 16% — even as the 12-month Euribor edges toward 3% and payments tick up. Yet top-end demand is white-hot: a €60M Foz tower sold out in 45 days, and a foreign trio just committed €87M to build 245 homes. Net: capital is abundant but choosy — asset quality, not sector, now separates winners from the rest.

editions.label: 10 Sep
editions.title: Portugal and EIB back 50,000 affordable homes with €1.5bn credit line
editions.summary: Portugal's housing story split in two this week. The Government and the European Investment Bank opened a €1.5 billion credit line — €500m signed as a first tranche — to finance roughly 50,000 affordable homes that fell outside the PRR. On the private side, foreign developer Nova Atlantic committed €87 million to 245 homes across Sintra, Gaia and Viana, while Pestana broke ground on 236 coastal units already 70% sold. But the cost of building it all keeps climbing: new-build construction costs rose 6.8% year-on-year in July, with copper wire up about 25%. Net: capital — public and private — is piling into Portuguese housing faster than the system can pour concrete.

editions.label: 09 Sep
editions.title: Foreign trio bets €87M on 245 Portuguese homes — outside Lisbon prime
editions.summary: Foreign capital is moving past Lisbon prime — and into the mid-market. A new three-founder firm, Nova Atlantic, is committing €87 million to build 245 homes across Sintra, Gaia and Viana do Castelo, with units from €165,000. In Porto, a design-led Foz tower (Belfoz) hit 100% reservations in 45 days. And from 1 September, Portugal's new affordable-rent regime hands landlords a full income-tax exemption if rents sit at or below 80% of the municipal median. Commercial investment, meanwhile, is running at €1.4 billion for the half-year — hotels leading, offices sliding. Net: the money is broadening — down the value chain, out of the capital, and increasingly shaped by tax policy.

editions.label: 08 Sep
editions.title: Spain's Alfana buys Forum Algarve for €130M — its first deal abroad
editions.summary: Alfana Investment Management is buying Forum Algarve for about €130 million — the Spanish manager's first-ever deal outside Spain. The Faro centre is a trophy: 27,400 sqm, 115 shops, near-100% occupancy and 7.8 million visitors a year. Santander private-wealth clients funded it, with the signing set for Lisbon this week. Elsewhere, capital keeps chasing scarce prime stock — Lisbon prime rents rose 7.6% in H1, second only to Cape Town worldwide. And the rulebook is shifting: the Bank of Portugal's new 45% loan-to-income cap took effect on 1 August, while a fresh decree overhauls public-works procurement from 1 October. Net: retail and residential are where conviction sits; regulation is the variable to watch.

editions.label: 07 Sep
editions.title: Portugal tops the world on house prices: +15.2%, No.1 of 57 economies
editions.summary: Portugal posted the world's steepest real house-price growth in Q1 — up 15.2% year-on-year, first of 57 economies tracked by the Bank for International Settlements. Globally, real prices actually fell 1.2%; the eurozone managed just 2.6%. Capital is following the heat: commercial investment hit €1.41bn in H1, up 14%, led by hotels at €508M. Lisbon apartments now average €5,850/m² (+16%), Porto €4,180 (+13%). Retail dealmaking is back too — Spain's Alfana bought Faro's Forum Algarve for €130M, its first move abroad. Net: demand still vastly outruns supply, and foreign money is leaning in, not out.

editions.label: 6 Sep
editions.title: Alfana buys Forum Algarve for €130M — Spain's first bet outside home turf
editions.summary: Spain's Alfana bought Forum Algarve for around €130M — its first deal outside its home market, and Commerz Real's exit from the 27,400 sqm Faro centre. Retail keeps proving it can move at scale even as prime offices stay starved of stock. In Lisbon, BPI Gestão de Ativos sold a Saldanha office block for residential conversion, the latest in a wave that turned roughly a fifth of 2025 office deals into change-of-use plays. On the supply side, BPI now expects 2026 home completions to hit a 16-year high near 27,900 units. Porto and Matosinhos are both leaning in, funding more than 2,000 affordable rental homes between them. Net: capital is chasing retail and hospitality while the housing machine finally speeds up — but prime offices remain the market's tightest squeeze.
